cells.tense: The hand has already decided, and it is still holding the pen.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Someone near you is carrying something heavy. Sit with them without fixing it. Let what they hold land on you a little, and keep your own footing while it does.
cells.core:
You can stand under something heavy without stiffening around it. That is not passivity — the load gets carried and the body stays open. Where you tend what matters, you put weight in and then let the result land where it lands. People feel they can lean in without getting squeezed.

But strength can go lonely when nothing is allowed to reach it. Someone near you is being managed rather than felt, and you keep just enough distance to stay steady. Let their load touch you this week and stay on your own feet anyway. A hand on your arm you do not shrug off, a story you do not redirect, a silence you let stay sad. You do not have to carry them. You just have to stop going numb in order to stay strong.
cells.sheetLine: You can keep your footing and still be moved by what they carry.
cells.verb: bearing what has to be borne until the bearing is done
cells.place: at the point where the grip is let go

cells.tense: The bracing is already happening for a week that has not arrived.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Look at what you are holding for other people. Give back what was not yours to carry, keep what is, then stop there. No tally of who owes what.
cells.core:
Endurance in the right amount is a floor. Too much and it turns to a vise — what is yours and what is not both end up gripped, and the grip starts to feel like the point. You brace for the next thing before the last one has finished, and people feel it. Steadiness starts reading as control, and it costs you the closeness you were trying to keep.

Proportion is the way back. Look honestly at what is in your hands — is all of this actually mine, and how much does it need today? Hold that much, then stop. Fairness here is not punishment; it is just the right size. One day at the correct weight teaches you what your arms have been doing. What belonged to someone else can go back to them without anyone being blamed.
cells.sheetLine: You are gripping harder than the thing requires.

cells.tense: The door closed, and the body is still standing in the doorway.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Something in your life is over, and part of you keeps tending it anyway — a message, a worry, a role you keep answering. Stop feeding that one for a while.
cells.core:
When the weight came, the strength went quiet. Holding anything after that felt like the very thing that had failed, and the hands learned to let go early, before a grip could form. That kept you moving. It also means things pass through without being carried, and you may notice you are not where you intended to be. A door behind you is still taking your weight.

Releasing on purpose is different from losing your grip. One thing has already ended and something in you refills it anyway. Stop feeding that one thing and watch where your weight goes instead. Empty hands are allowed to stay empty. That is not defeat, and it is not the pause before some next noble carry. It is just empty, and that is allowed.
cells.sheetLine: You let go before you got to hold it.

cells.tense: The hand is doing the work, and the name on it has gone missing.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Out of everything you are holding, pick the one that matters most to you, and turn toward it this week. Whatever has been pulling at you can wait its turn.
cells.core:
You are bearing a lot, and none of it feels authored by you. When it holds, you credit the timing or the people around. When it gives way, you take the whole blame. Either way you are watching rather than doing — the strength and the collapse running without your hand in them. Nobody asked what you wanted, so the asking stopped.

Wanting is not selfish, and it does not have to become a plan. Out of everything you are carrying, choose the one that matters most, and turn toward it this week. No chasing, no announcing. Let it be wanted, to yourself, and see how the weight feels once it has a direction pointing somewhere you picked. You were already steering by something. This just lets you face it on purpose.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose the direction. You just don't count it as yours.
